drafted_by: Claude (session agent), on operator request to push ahead on A-pool-frontend
standing_rule: Prose without a failing test always loses to a convenient default.
question: Holding the frontend architecture fixed at EquiformerPoolFrontend (cold_init, no MPtrj ckpt), does raising lr_frontend from the sealed 1e-5 to 1e-4 clear the already-locked M2 macro-F1 train + held-out capacity bars over the full 12-fold LOSO -- and does the sealed-matched 1e-5 arm, on the same real frontend, reproduce the SE(3)-lite card's stuck floor?

why_this_card.prior_scope_gap: Sealed M2 card's SE(3)-lite frontend only executes backbone.blocks[0] (see lesson L-se3-lite-frontend-1-of-7-blocks) -- it could never test frontend-architecture capacity regardless of LR.
why_this_card.diagnostic_motivation: scripts/diag_gradflow_pool_frontend.py, 4 of 12 train structures, 200 of 400 steps: at lr_frontend=1e-5 reproduced the sealed card's exact stuck floor (min_f1 0.327/0.324 vs sealed ~0.31-0.33); at lr_frontend=1e-4, all 4 structures cleared with real minority-class discrimination (train macro_f1 0.895, min_f1 0.865), including the structure pinned at exact majority under 1e-5 (1TEN:A acc=maj=0.933/lift=1.000/f1=0.32 -> acc=0.989/lift=1.060/f1=0.887) -- ruling out majority-sharpening as the explanation.
why_this_card.diagnostic_caveat_carried_forward: That diagnostic used only 4 of 12 structures (76-155 residues) -- specifically 3 of the 4 lowest-held-out-F1 folds in the sealed 12-fold M2 result (1UBQ 0.307, 1TEN 0.316, 1LYZ 0.317; 1HHP 0.320 mid-pack) -- so it is train-fit-only evidence on historically hard-to-generalize structures, not a held-out result. This card exists to get the held-out answer.
why_this_card.governed_frontend_note: Unlike the SE(3)-lite pilots, this card's frontend is real (EquiformerPoolFrontend, cold_init) and assert_governed_assembly runs with allow_off_path_frontend=False -- pure_hyp_pass is a live enforced gate here, not skipped. Spot-checked clean ahead of time (scripts/diag_gradflow_pool_frontend.py --mode verify-pure-hyp, 0 violations) but re-checked live in every fold's run_one_fold, not assumed.

isolation_discipline.rule: Exactly one variable changes between arms: lr_frontend. Frontend architecture, cold_init, max_neighbors, activation checkpointing, sdrp_coeff, seed, steps, folds, moe_mode, and lr_hyperbolic are identical across both arms.

sealed.purpose: control -- same frontend architecture as lr_1e-4 arm, sealed-matched LR

lr_1e-4.purpose: primary -- the arm the pool-frontend diagnostic motivated

isolation_discipline.amendment_rule: Any change to locked bars, steps, seed, frontend, max_neighbors, or the two LR values requires a new signed card, not an edit to this one.

design.purpose_class: harness_capacity_G_fit_M2 -- intentional leak; not biology; not defect-B close

frontend.activation_checkpointing: gradient_checkpointing_block_list = [1]*7 on the backbone -- required to fit a 4GB GPU; verified bit-equivalent to no-checkpointing (max abs grad diff 4.5e-8 over 318 tensors, scripts/diag_gradflow_pool_frontend.py --mode verify-checkpoint)
frontend.se3_lite: FORBIDDEN on this card (that is the entire point of it)

protocol.split: LOSO 12 folds -- folds_frozen.json (same folds as the sealed M2 card)
protocol.device_stop: If CUDA unavailable: STOP. No CPU fallback.

pass_fail_bars.status: REUSED VERBATIM from the sealed M2 card -- not re-derived, since the target/reachability geometry (SDRP label distribution) is unchanged; only the frontend and lr_frontend differ
pass_fail_bars.G_finite: no non-finite loss or gradient in any fold

G_fit_train.metric: per-structure train macro-F1 at last step
G_fit_train.bar: macro-mean over the 11 train structures >= 0.40 AND min train-structure macro-F1 >= 0.40

S1_mean_macro_f1.bar: mean over the 12 held-out structures of macro-F1 >= 0.40

verdict_table.INCONCLUSIVE_UNDERFIT: G_finite and G_grad_spine pass; G_fit_train fails
verdict_table.FAIL_NO_SIGNAL: G_finite and G_grad_spine and G_fit_train pass; S1 or S2 fails
verdict_table.PASS_SIGNAL: all gates -- capacity probe only; see not_claims

compute_budget.status: BLOCKING -- scope not yet authorized, see open_decision below

benchmark.hardware: single 4GB GPU (Quadro T1000), the only GPU available in this environment
benchmark.method: scripts/bench_pool_frontend_step_time.py --hold 1MBN:A --steps 25 (committed, re-runnable; originally a /tmp script -- see lesson L-tmp-scripts-not-durable in data/gates/tokyo_eye_equ_agenda.json)
benchmark.result: 31.5s/step (stddev ~0.06s, flat), peak memory 3.18GB flat from step 1 through step 24 -- no fragmentation growth observed over 25 steps

compute_budget.risk_note: step-count reduction is not free: the pool-frontend diagnostic at lr=1e-4 stayed flat at the majority-basin F1 level through step ~80-120 before climbing to its final value by step 199 (on smaller, easier structures than several of these 12 folds) -- fewer than ~150-200 steps risks an underpowered INCONCLUSIVE_UNDERFIT read that reflects compute-starvation, not capacity, and 400 steps also keeps this card comparable step-for-step to the sealed lite M2 card.
compute_budget.open_decision: RESOLVED 2026-09-22 (operator 'go' in session chat, on the agent's recommended default): run lr_1e-4 arm alone first, full locked 400 steps, all 12 folds (~42h). sealed (1e-5) control arm deferred to a follow-up run pending this arm's result.
compute_budget.background_execution_note: runs incrementally -- each completed fold's JSON is written to data/gates/wrap1_zhyp_m2_pool_lr/<arm>/ immediately, and the runner skips folds that already have a result file on restart, so a long background run surviving across sessions loses at most the in-progress fold if interrupted.
